correctness.rationale: For h_j in (0,1) the survival probabilities are positive at every finite age. The last-reset partition gives Φ_t(X)=S_t E^t(X)+Tr(X)B_t with Tr B_t=1−S_t. Setting q_t=S_{t+1}/S_t and subtracting q_t E(B_t) from B_{t+1} gives a mass ν_{t+1} at σ and coefficients ν_s S_{t−s}(h_{t+1}−h_{t+1−s}) at E^{t+1−s}(σ). Hence for nondecreasing hazards Y_t≥0 with trace h_{t+1}. The intermediate is a convex combination of E and a replacement channel and the composition identity holds without assuming E invertible. For the converse use a cyclic unitary and pure reset at site zero with dimension m+2 for a drop at m. The trace-preserving Φ_m has trivial kernel because on traceless operators it is S_m times a unitary conjugation, so the intermediate is unique. Only the age-m term contributes at site m and the test projector at m is moved to site m+1 by the unitary. The intermediate therefore has the negative site-m entry h_1S_{m−1}(h_{m+1}−h_m). I separately propagated exact age-and-site probabilities for drops at m=1,2,6: from each initial site advance mass by (1−h_{age+1}) to (age+1, next site) and by h_{age+1} to (0,0); sum over ages to form T_m,T_{m+1}, and multiply T_{m+1}T_m⁻¹. For h_j=2/5 up to m and h_{m+1}=1/5 the predicted negative entry is −(2/25)(3/5)^{m−1}; for m=1 the test column is (7/25,−2/25,4/5). The simulations corroborate the all-time operator argument. The frozen checker counts a separate m=1 example in addition to positions 1–14, so its fifteen witness checks do not mean fifteen distinct positions.
residual_risks: This is a universal Schrödinger-picture equivalence, not an iff for an individual update and reset state. It makes no minimal-dimension or process-tensor claim.
